back: The combination of product, price, promotion and place decisions (plus people, processes and physical evidence for services).
People, processes and physical evidence are added to the 4Ps.
A feature that makes a product different from and better than competing products in customers' eyes.
Making a product different from rivals' products in a way customers value.
Recognition, loyalty, a price premium, trust and a platform for new products.
Protect, preserve, inform, promote, give convenience and position the product.
Goods are tangible and can be stored; services are intangible and cannot be stored.
Product, price, promotion and place all support the same target market and positioning.
